briefing.title: Briefing after cycle 010 — what the world is pressing on

question: Which of these two should the world act on first, in the coming year?

matters.title: The war on Iran and the Strait of Hormuz
matters.gist: The US and Israel went to war on Iran on 28 February 2026, and Iran closed the strait that carries much of the world's oil and gas.

matters.title: The energy shock as a cost-of-living crisis
matters.gist: The IMF expects 4.7 % inflation in 2026 and links cost-of-living crises to worsening inequality and poverty.

matters.title: Hunger under war and funding cuts
matters.gist: FAO and WFP name 13 hunger hotspots for June to November 2026, with a risk of famine in 14 areas of Sudan, while funding for food aid has fallen steeply.

matters.title: A very strong El Niño on record-warm oceans
matters.gist: Sea surface temperatures set a September record, and the coming El Niño is likely to be one of the strongest ever measured.

matters.title: COP31, Antalya, 9 to 20 November
matters.gist: Turkey hosts the climate conference and Australia presides over the talks; adaptation, a just transition and the roadmaps away from fossil fuels are on the table.

matters.title: Wars that returned this autumn
matters.gist: Ethiopia is back at war after a TPLF offensive, the Houthis advanced on Yemen's Red Sea coast and shelled Saudi Arabia, and Pakistan struck Afghanistan again.

matters.title: Ebola in eastern Congo
matters.gist: A Bundibugyo-virus outbreak declared in mid-May became the second largest Ebola outbreak on record; most admitted patients were not known contacts.

matters.title: AI and the first rung of work
matters.gist: In the occupations most exposed to AI, employment of workers aged 22 to 25 is 19 % below that of their peers.

matters.title: Elections and synthetic media
matters.gist: The US votes on 3 November; AI deepfakes have appeared in campaigns, and the WEF ranks mis- and disinformation second among the risks of the next two years.

matters.title: Biodiversity loss and the Earth's systems, over ten years
matters.gist: Over ten years, the WEF's experts rank extreme weather, biodiversity loss and critical change to Earth systems first to third.
